judge_assessment.explanation: Independently confirmed against worksheet.tex and verify.json: the grid plots A(2,7), B(7,2), C(5,4), D(4,5), so C to D is |5-4|+|4-5| = 2 steps (p1) and Nia's (7,2) to the intended (2,7) is 5+5 = 10 steps (p2) with B and A the two labelled points, exactly as the key says. Pattern X = 0,3,6,9,12 against Y = 0,1,2,3,4 gives up-value 12/3 = 4 (p3). The bean-plant plot's stacks are 3,5,4,2,1, so four plants are 3 in tall (p4), the mode is 2 1/2 in (p5) and 15 plants were measured (p6). Pattern A's fourth term is 7 and B's is 21 (p7). Problem 8 is correctly typed manual with a desc that lists what full credit needs. Two things the judge did not check. Problem 7(c) asks the student to 'write the 4th ordered pair correctly and say what Sam did' -- a diagnosis -- and verify.json id 7 holds only the two eval entries, so the same sheet that flags problem 8 leaves 7(c) unflagged. And problem 2 prints two more answers than are checked: 'Which labelled point did Nia land on, and which one did she mean?' (B and A in the key) sits beside a single eval entry for the 10-step distance.

strengths_to_preserve: Every one of the eight declared traps is a specific misread rather than arithmetic noise, and the key prints them as a mapped list: 0 (decided reversed pairs must be the same point), 5 (counted only the sideways move), 12 (gave the across-value when asked for the up-value), 3 (copied the height printed under the marks), 5 again (counted marks instead of naming the height), 21 and 7 (put the wrong pattern's term first). A wrong answer on this sheet names the misconception by itself.

The line-plot data lives once, as {2:3, 2.5:5, 3:4, 3.5:2, 4:1} in verify.json, and drives both the drawn stacks and the read_data / stats checks, so the picture and the key cannot drift apart -- which is exactly what a scale-misreading sheet must not get wrong.

Problem 8's manual desc is a usable rubric rather than a shrug: both points plotted and labelled, a sentence saying the first number counts across and the second up, and a memory aid; and the key supplies three aids ('along the hall, then up the stairs') plus a fallback for the child who insists the two points are the same.

root_causes.description: An explanation sub-part attached to a problem that already has machine entries is not required to be typed `manual`, so the same sheet flags problem 8 and silently ships problem 7(c)'s diagnosis as verified work.
evidence: worksheet.pdf p4 problem 7(c): 'Write the 4th ordered pair correctly and say what Sam did.'
verify.json id 7 holds two eval entries (2n-1 = 7 and 6n-3 = 21) and no manual entry
answer_key.pdf p3 answers it in prose: 'Sam wrote (21, 7) -- both numbers are right, but he put Pattern B's term first'
verify.json id 8 IS typed manual with a full rubric, so the convention exists and was simply not applied to 7(c)

root_causes.description: Coverage is counted per id, so problem 2's two point-name answers -- machine-checkable against the same labelled-point data that draws the grid -- carry no entry.
evidence: worksheet.pdf p2 problem 2: 'Which labelled point did Nia land on, and which one did she mean?' before the step count
verify.json id 2 holds one eval entry, Abs(h-p)+Abs(k-q) = 10
answer_key.pdf p2 supplies both names ('lands on the point labelled B ... the point she meant ... is labelled A')
worksheet.tex lines 34-41 already hold the labelled coordinates A(2,7), B(7,2), C(5,4), D(4,5) that a read_data check could use

improvements.title: Flag problem 7(c)'s 'say what Sam did' diagnosis as manual review
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual-coverage gate to the build chain. A new checker (tests/check_manual_coverage.py, wired into scripts/build.sh beside answer-line-ws) segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.py and, for each problem, scans the printed prose for open-response cues -- 'Explain', 'Why did/does', 'Say why', 'What went wrong', 'describe', 'in one or two sentences', 'Which ... did/was' followed by a rule blank, and the drawing verbs 'Plot', 'Shade', 'Draw', 'label' -- and requires the matching id in verify.json to carry at least one entry of type 'manual'. Exit 1 with the offending sentence quoted when it does not. SKILL.md line 257 already states the rule ('Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer'); nothing enforces it, and per-problem coverage (SKILL.md line 189) is satisfied by any single machine entry on the same id.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_manual_coverage.py gains a fixture from problem 7: a segment ending 'Write the 4th ordered pair correctly and say what Sam did' with a verify.json id 7 holding two eval entries. Assert the checker exits 1 and quotes the clause; add a manual entry and assert exit 0. The current chain reports this sheet as green with one manual item, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: A misconception-analysis sheet reports the number of diagnoses a human must read (2) rather than the number that happened to lack a numeric companion (1). Across the suite this is the second-largest cluster (36 cases).
improvements.risk: The cue 'say what X did' is close to phrasing used in ordinary numeric problems; narrow the rule to clauses that follow a correct-answer request, and keep manual items at exit 2 so the build still ships.

improvements.title: Check the two labelled-point answers in problem 2
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the sheet-side gate so coverage is counted per printed response slot, not per problem id. tests/check_answer_line.py already segments the worksheet and reads verify.json; have it also count the response slots each segment prints (\ansblank, \answerline, \ansline, and \underline{\hspace{...}}) and fail when a problem prints more slots than its id has verify entries, unless the surplus is explicitly absorbed by a 'manual' entry. SKILL.md's JSON-format section should state the rule as 'one check per printed blank', replacing today's 'at least one check per problem id'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_unit_binding.py gains a fixture from problem 2: a segment asking which labelled point Nia landed on and which she meant, then how many steps apart they are, against a verify.json id 2 with one eval entry. Assert exit 1 naming the two uncovered slots; add read_data entries over the labelled-point map ({'A': '(2,7)', 'B': '(7,2)', ...}) and assert exit 0. No slot count exists today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The two point names the key already prints become machine-proved from the same coordinates that draw the grid, which is the one place this sheet could silently disagree with its own picture.
improvements.risk: Naming answers are strings, so the entry has to be a read_data lookup rather than an expression; keep the map small and derived from the figure data to avoid a second source of truth.

case_summary: Eight misconception-analysis items on coordinates, line plots and pattern pairs. All arithmetic verified here from the artifacts: 2 and 10 grid steps, 12/3 = 4, four plants at 3 in, mode 2 1/2 in, 15 plants, fourth terms 7 and 21. The traps are the strongest feature -- eight declared, each a named misread, all printed in the key as a common-wrong-answer map -- and the line-plot data drives both the drawing and the checks, so picture and key cannot diverge. The ACCEPT is right. The gap is labelling: problem 8 is typed manual with a real rubric while problem 7(c)'s 'say what Sam did' diagnosis is recorded as fully machine-checked, and problem 2's two point-name answers have no entry. final_response.md names the three documents by role and describes each, though unlike eight of its siblings it prints no filenames -- worth aligning, but it does surface all three artifacts, so the surfacing issue does not apply.
